extracted.intended_audience: students and educators learning or teaching mathematics (math learners, expositors)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for learners (and those who write about math) on techniques and attitudes that produce deep conceptual understanding rather than rote proficiency. Emphasises active grappling, multiple-perspective analysis, and exposition that forces thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core principle: grapple with the mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: To fully understand a piece of mathematics, you have to grapple with it; you must work hard to fully understand every aspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding requires active effort — passively reading or following steps is insufficient. Spend time wrestling with ideas until they make sense in multiple ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse from multiple angles
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine concepts from every side, as if inspecting an object (e.g., a phone) from all sides to understand its complete structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use different representations, examples, special cases, and equivalent formulations to build a richer picture of the concept; avoid relying on a single perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate foundational ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and probe the core principles underlying mathematical concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace results back to their basic assumptions and primitives; understanding the foundations clarifies why results hold and how they connect to other ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask critical questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Constantly ask what mathematical objects have in common and why definitions/theorems are stated the way they are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions like 'What is it that they all have in common?' help expose unifying structures and reveal deeper insight; interrogate definitions and hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Struggle intentionally
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberately wrestle with mathematical ideas (purposeful struggle) to internalise them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace productive difficulty rather than avoiding it; targeted problem-solving and attempts before looking at solutions promote retention and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise understanding over speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Value comprehension and clarity above rapid computation or quick completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slow down when necessary to make sense of steps and concepts; depth of understanding is more important than finishing quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't memorise mechanically
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid rote memorisation of formulas or procedures without grasping underlying concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memorisation without understanding leads to fragile knowledge; instead, learn why formulas work and when to apply them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't treat math as mere symbol-manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not reduce mathematics to arithmetic or notation alone; it involves deep ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the conceptual meaning behind symbols and manipulations, not just the mechanical steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't rush the learning process
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding takes time and cannot be reliably accelerated without sacrificing depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for grappling and revisiting ideas; impatience tends to produce superficial knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall philosophy: move from passive following to active thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning math means transitioning from passive symbol-following to active, clear thinking about mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to 'see' mathematics with genuine clarity rather than merely reproducing procedures; cultivate habits that encourage independent thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implication for good math writing: slow the reader and force grappling
rubrics_metrics.description: A good exposition slows the reader down, forces grappling, and reveals the underlying ideas rather than presenting symbol-manipulation as a finished script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing or teaching, structure exposition to highlight ideas, motivate definitions/theorems, provide multiple perspectives and encourage active engagement rather than offering only polished computations.
